summary:
Most agricultural tools ask, "What should I plant this year?" BasinShift asks, "What survives your worst drought year without draining the aquifer?" Built for the Field Shift challenge, BasinShift stress-tests a farmer's 4-year crop rotation plan across 41 historical 4-year periods (1982–2025) and 2040s climate projections (NEX-GDDP-CMIP6) using real NASA Earth observation data.

Instead of relying on averages, we evaluate all 20,736 possible 4-year crop sequences (12 crops) through daily FAO-56 Penman-Monteith water balance and FAO-33 yield response models. The engine enforces 2026 Konya Closed Basin water-restriction and crop-rotation regulations (flagging yellow/red card subsidy penalties) alongside farmer-specific constraints (equipment, contracts, water quotas). From the Pareto frontier, it recommends three transparent, justified options—Profit, Aquifer, and Balance—with explicit data provenance and confidence labels. Finally, a basin-scale linear programming model (HiGHS) calculates the "price of anarchy," shadow water price, and cooperative profit-sharing so individual decisions do not collapse the shared groundwater aquifer.
details:
What It Does & How It Works BasinShift is a two-scale agricultural decision-support platform operating at both the field level and the shared groundwater basin level. Using the Konya Closed Basin (Türkiye)—home to 739 sinkholes and a ~30 m groundwater drop since the 1980s—as our primary pilot, our calculation pipeline runs in under 2 seconds per field:

  1. Climate & Bias Correction: Fetches daily meteorological data (1981–2026) from NASA POWER and corrects its ~60% precipitation overestimation in Konya using monthly ratios from GPM IMERG satellite precipitation, bringing annual rainfall in line with local station normals (~316–327 mm).
  2. Agronomic & Risk Simulation: Simulates all 20,736 4-year combinations of 12 crops across 41 rolling 4-year historical windows (preserving multi-year droughts like 2007–2008). Daily root-zone water balance (FAO-56) and yield response (FAO-33) are paired with heat/frost stress, 200 Monte Carlo market price volatility scenarios, and 2026 water-restriction subsidy rules (YAML rule engine).
  3. Pareto Optimization & Explainability: Filters out rule-violating or equipment-constrained plans and computes a multi-objective Pareto frontier (Average Profit, Worst-5% CVaR Income, Irrigation Water, and Soil Health). It presents three justified cards (Profit, Aquifer, Balance) with a 1-page printable Turkish/English PDF Risk & Water Scorecard. In our Çumra benchmark (120 da), the Balance plan cuts water use by 58% (-574 m³/da/yr), doubles worst-period income (CVaR 5%), avoids red-card subsidy loss (+1,248 TRY/da), and withstands +2 °C and 2040s CMIP6 warming.
  4. Basin-Scale Coordination: Uses Linear Programming (SciPy HiGHS) and a Cobweb price-feedback model alongside GRACE/GRACE-FO total water storage trends (-1.0 cm/yr) to quantify the cost of uncoordinated farming, the marginal shadow price of water (9.54 TRY/m³), and cooperative compensation mechanisms.

Tools, Languages & Architecture Built in Python 3.11+ with a decoupled engine (basinshift/) and Streamlit UI (app.py), utilizing NumPy, Pandas, SciPy (HiGHS), Plotly, and fpdf2. Includes 80 automated unit/validation tests (pytest) verifying FAO-56 textbook benchmarks, Mann-Kendall trend tests, rule logic, and strict data provenance (KAYNAK.yaml).

Creativity, Transparency & Design Factors Unlike black-box AI predictors, every number in BasinShift is traceable to physical formulas and accompanied by explicit confidence dots and provenance tags. Four datasets are live/verified NASA products (POWER, GPM IMERG, GRACE/GRACE-FO, NEX-GDDP-CMIP6), while unretrieved AppEEARS layers (SMAP, HLS/MODIS NDVI, SRTM) are transparently labeled as synthetic placeholders or assumptions and excluded from core water/profit calculations. The engine is modular and already configured for Konya, California's Central Valley, Punjab, and the Murray-Darling Basin.
